names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 8 octombrie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Οκτωβρίου, «Οσία Πελαγία», with the rank word left off. The page glosses the name from πέλαγος, the open sea.

The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2641 and the heading of both of its lives for her, «Преподобная Пелагия Антиохийская», with the rank word and the epithet left off. The longer life gives «Пелагея» beside it and is not followed.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 8. октобар ст. ст., „Преп. Пелагија.“ — Преп. is the venerable grade this corpus puts in `types` and comes off, so the bare forename is the whole of the form. **The Prologue gives her no epithet and no city**, so there is nothing fuller to store, and the day’s third entry gives the other Pelagia the same bare string. `foldchk.py` measured this form before the day as held by `pelagia-of-caesarea-in-palestine` alone, off the Prologue’s heading for the Julian 25 March; the fold is three folders now and is read in the `serbian` row’s note and in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`.

source.note: The rank is the alt text of the day's one icon, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service marked with no sign in the Typikon, which is the plain service. It stands immediately before her line, and her line is the only one in its paragraph. The day's service block names her and nobody else, «8 октября: Преподобной матери нашей Пелаги».

attestations.note: Her name page lists this one day and no other. The site's two lives for her disagree twice over and neither is preferred: the shorter makes Nonnus bishop of Edessa and puts her over the dancing-women of Antioch in Palestine, the longer makes him bishop of Heliopolis and has her born in Antioch in Syria. Both end her on the Mount of Olives under the man's name Pelagius, and the folder's `dates` carry the 457 they share.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul pe 8 octombrie — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Pelaghia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Οκτωβρίου — «Οσία Πελαγία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same woman: the harlot of Antioch converted by the preaching of the bishop Nonnus, baptised, and gone eight days later to Jerusalem. saint.gr gives no year, so no `dates` object is proposed. The same day page carries a second and different Pelagia, «Αγία Πελαγία η Παρθένος», who is drafted as a new folder in this batch. The page prints a proper apolytikion in the fourth tone and a kontakion, both taken here; it also prints an «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον», the common «Ἐν σοὶ Μῆτερ» for a venerable woman, and an Οἶκος and a Κάθισμα, none of which is drafted. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page refers the reader to Nonnus at 10 Νοεμβρίου; the corpus holds no Nonnus folder, so nothing is linked.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.10.2026 (8. октобар ст. ст.) — „Преп. Пелагија.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted whole, **with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints**, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN §4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because `srbody.mjs` and `sr-cand.mjs` both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends `. ` in the source. **An earlier wave of this reading quoted off the stripped output and wrote into its notes that the headings carry no closing stop, which the raw page contradicts for its own days as well as for these** — the rows of that wave are outside this reader’s range and are a finding for the author, not something fixed here. THE PENITENT, AND THE PROLOGUE SEPARATES THE TWO WOMEN ITSELF by giving her Преп., venerable, and the day’s third entry муч., martyr — two commemorations on one calendar means two women, and this book makes the distinction in its own rank words. She is the harlot of Antioch who heard bishop Nonnus preach in the church of the holy martyr Julian, was baptised, gave away her wealth and shut herself up on the Mount of Olives as the monk Pelagius: the folder that exists, and no arrival. `dates` WIDENED, AND THIS IS THE ONE DATE CHANGE OF THE DAY. The folder held `death` 457 flat, off the Russian day line «Прп. Пелагии (457)» and both its Russian lives; this entry closes «Упокоји се св. Пелагија око 461. год.», about 461. **Two books give two years, so the interval is widened to carry both and chooses neither** — 457 or 461, which is «X or Y» and not a narrowing, and is the shape the day’s other Pelagia already carries for «284 or 303». Both years are in the note, each with the book that prints it. `types` UNTOUCHED at `venerable`, corroborated by Преп. WHAT IS NEW ON A 7 kB LIFE that already holds the Romanian, the Greek and two Russian accounts. Her own words at the bishop’s feet, which no other book read for this folder gives: „Смилуј се мени, грешној, оче свети, крсти ме и научи ме покајању: ја сам море безакоња, амбис пропасти, мрежа и оруђе ђаволско.“ — a sea of iniquities, an abyss of perdition, a net and an instrument of the devil. The longer Russian life has her say her sins outnumbered the sand of the sea, which is a different sentence. And the end is told differently: **the deacon James buries her himself**, finding her alive at the first visit and dead a few days later at the second, where the Romanian life has the patriarch of Jerusalem come with a crowd to anoint the body and the sex discovered at the anointing. The Prologue also makes James explicitly **Nonnus’s deacon**. NO NEW `related` AND TWO NAMES DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN INTO THE PROSE. `nonnus-the-bishop` is already there and is the one person of the entry who has a folder. The deaconess Романа who stood godmother at the baptism **has no folder in this corpus and gets none from a reader** — Ruling 3 — and nor does the deacon Јаков; the existing life names both already, without rows, because `related-floor.test.mjs` matches a display name exactly and nothing is displayed as «Romana» or «James». The church of the martyr Julian is a dedication and not a relation. **The entry opens by setting her beside the day’s other penitent and the comparison takes no row and no name**: sharing a day is not a relation. No `locations`, no `office`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE FOLD THIS DAY MADE, AND IT IS THREE FOLDERS. The Prologue gives **neither** Pelagia an epithet — the two headings are «Преп. Пелагија» and «Св. муч. Пелагија» — so the bare forename is what the source gives and both folders take the same string, the way both already share the Russian «Пелагия». `foldchk.py` measured «Пелагија» **before** this day as `[('pelagia-of-caesarea-in-palestine', 'sr')]` — one folder already held it, off the Prologue’s own heading for the Julian 25 March, so this day widens the fold from one folder to three and not from nothing to two. The READ_FOLDS key `пелагија pelagia-of-antioch pelagia-of-caesarea-in-palestine pelagia-the-virgin-of-antioch` is added to `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in the same commit, because reading a fold is two acts.

hymns.text: Întru tine, maică, cu osârdie s-a mântuit cel după chip; că, luând crucea, ai urmat lui Hristos; şi lucrând, ai învăţat să nu se uite la trup, căci este trecător; ci să poarte grijă de suflet, de lucrul cel nemuritor. Pentru aceasta şi cu îngerii împreună se bucură, Cuvioasă Maică Pelaghia, duhul tău.

english.text: In thee, O mother, was that which is according to the image kept safe with diligence; for taking up the cross thou didst follow Christ, and in thy labour thou didst teach us to overlook the flesh, since it passeth away, and to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Wherefore thy spirit, O venerable mother Pelagia, rejoiceth together with the angels.

hymns.text: Ἐξ ἀκανθῶν καθάπερ ρόδον εὐῶδες, τὴ Ἐκκλησία Πελαγία ἐδείχθης, ταὶς ἐναρέτοις πράξεσιν εὐφραίνουσα ἠμᾶς, ὅθεν καὶ προσήγαγες, ὡς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, τῷ σὲ θαυμαστώσαντι, τὸν σὸν βίον Ὁσία. Ὂν ἐκδυσώπει σώζεσθαι ἠμᾶς, παθῶν παντοίων, ψυχῆς τὲ καὶ σώματος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ὁ ὑψωθεὶς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ — the first hymn on the page of «Οσία Πελαγία», and it names her. The «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον» printed under it is the common «Ἐν σοὶ Μῆτερ» for a venerable woman and is not drafted.

english.text: Like a sweet-smelling rose out of thorns you were shown to the Church, Pelagia, gladdening us by your virtuous deeds; and so you brought your life, as a scent of sweetness, to him who made you wonderful. Entreat him that we be saved from every passion of soul and body.

hymns.text: Τὸ σῶμα τὸ σὸν νηστείαις κατατήξασα, ἀγρύπνοις εὐχαῖς, τὸv Κτίστην καθικέτευες, τοῦ λαβεῖν σῶν πράξεων, τὴv τελείαν Μῆτερ συγχώρησιv, ἢν καὶ ἔλαβες ἀληθῶς, ὁδὸν μετανοίας ὑποδείξασα.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — on the page of «Οσία Πελαγία». It is addressed to her as Μῆτερ and names no other saint. The Οἶκος printed under it, which does name her, and the Κάθισμα below it are not kinds the schema holds and are not drafted.

english.text: Having wasted your body with fasting, you besought the Creator with sleepless prayers to receive the perfect forgiveness of your deeds, mother; and you truly received it, having shown us the road of repentance.

death.note: Two books give two years and neither is preferred. The Russian calendar’s day line prints «Прп. Пелагии (457)» and both of its lives for her give that year, «до самой кончины (457) подвизалась в затворе» on the shorter and «инок Пелагий скончался приблизительно в 457 году» on the longer. The Ohrid Prologue for the Julian 8 October ends «Упокоји се св. Пелагија око 461. год.», about 461. The interval spans both. Neither saint.gr nor doxologia.ro was read for a year.
